_doc: Your own maps (maps/build_map.sh). source: the model; track_material: the racing surface (its centreline gives the road logic); road_materials: asphalt used for the width; drop: materials removed (sky backdrop); tags: CARLA semantic groups by material; start: where the hero spawns (CARLA coordinates, set from the start line). / 自作マップの設定 keep_left: traffic drives on the left (Japan): pods park in the left-most lane. Do not mark keep-left maps rule="LHT" in the OpenDRIVE when the lanes already run the way the cars go (netconvert --lefthand). left_hand_traffic: only for maps that do use CARLA's rule="LHT" lanes; run_pipeline turns hybrid physics off there (the traffic manager moves far-away cars the wrong way on them). buildings_csv: building table (x_east_m, y_north_m, height_m, footprint_m2) for maps whose buildings are not tagged Buildings; delivery_sim uses it for addresses, drone obstacles and the dashboard map.

pasir_ris._doc: Pasir Ris, Singapore: generated from OpenStreetMap by maps/make_osm_city.sh (osm_city/*). Keep-left. Road logic and 3-D model come from the same lanes; a ring road runs round the inside of the OSM box and along the near side of the Tampines Expressway.
pasir_ris.name: PasirRis

oita_kosen._doc: Oita Kosen (Akeno, Oita, Japan): generated from OpenStreetMap by the carla-map-generator skill, with terrain elevation from topoexport (GSI/PLATEAU) GLB. Keep-left. Landmarks: Oita Kosen school, its Akeno dormitory, the 7-Eleven down the road. OSM = the user's export (map (5).osm) merged with an OSM API strip to 33.2288 N for the 7-Eleven (osm_south/south.osm, 2026-11-02); terrain south of the main topoexport comes from the user's add-on export (238C9F, 33.2255-33.2316 N, 131.6475-131.6554 E).
oita_kosen.name: OitaKosen
oita_kosen._ring_speed_doc: the outer ring road's limit (osm_city/jp_speeds.py, with 274 posts after every joining street); the other roads keep their real limit (JARTIC zones, real OSM maxspeed, else the legal 60 with a centre line / 30 without). The user asked for it 2026-11-06
oita_kosen._signal_timing_doc: run_pipeline.py starts signal_timing.py apply --watch on this map: the Oita police (JARTIC type C) cycle and green/yellow/all-red by weekday/holiday and 5-minute slot, re-applied every slot (the user asked for it at every start, 2026-11-06)
oita_kosen._ring_guardrail_doc: white W-beam guardrail (props.py) 0.5 m behind the ring road's outer kerb, all the way round: the user asked for a barrier so cars cannot drive onto the grass outside the ring (2026-11-04)

area_features._doc: What stands on the main road between the 7-Eleven and Oita Kosen that OSM does not have (z20 tiles 2026, Google Earth, the user's photo of 2026-11-04: build/OitaKosen/seven_area_photos; osm_city/landmarks/akeno.py, lon/lat): greenhouses: multi-span vinyl houses on the farmland ways 184179075/77/79/80/83 and 184452633 (OSM farmland only), one platform each, ridge ns/ew, span/eave/rise m; farm_ground: their soil tracks; tree_rows: dense evergreen rows (camphor ~7 m) along the main road's west kerb (kept 6.6 m off the carriageway, off the footway) and the windbreak between the ranges; sand_pitch: Oita Kosen ground 2 (OSM pitch 152626821 has no surface/sport): sand, football lines (centre and goal lines read on the z20 tile), goals, the 12 m ball-stop net on its west and south sides, 2 m chain-link on the rest, along the platform edge (OSM fence way 182813888 lies in the footway band on the south); car_parks: the asphalt car park where 住友化学 明野台社宅S-1 (182819843, demolished) stood, bay rows = aisle-side edge, bays to its left/right
